question: Is any NEW hydrogen salt cavern actually being leached in Germany (not a conversion, not a plan)? What does the first new-build project imply for R07/R08?
finding: None found. Operating or near-term German H2 cavern projects are conversions of existing gas caverns (H2CAST Etzel: 2 caverns filled with ~90 t H2 from 9 May 2025; EWE Huntorf: 'eine von sieben unterirdischen Erdgaskavernen', H2 from end-2027, IPCEI). Small pilot caverns (Uniper Krummhoern, EWE Ruedersdorf) not checked here. The first new-build is Storengy SaltHy (Harsefeld): first borehole planned 2026, leaching 2027-2032, operation 2032, second cavern 2034.

quotes: etwa 7.000 Tonnen Wasserstoff gespeichert werden koennen
Die Abteufung der ersten Bohrung ist fuer 2026 geplant
2027-2032 erfolgt die Kavernensolung der ersten Wasserstoff-Salzkaverne
sources.note: quotes via page summariser, umlauts flattened; re-check against the page before citing
Etzel conversion, ~90 t H2 in 2 caverns (secondary reporting; not quoted)

consequence: Two corrections pull in opposite directions. Purpose-built H2 caverns may hold ~1.2-2x a converted gas cavern, cutting the R07 count from ~100 to ~55-84. But the first-of-kind schedule is ~5 yr of leaching (not R08b's 1.3 yr) and ~6 yr borehole-to-operation, so a restart starting 2026 delivers its first new cavern ~2032; at boom pace (11/yr) 55-84 caverns arrive ~2037-2040. Annual brine volume is unchanged by duration (set by caverns/yr x cavity); concurrency rises ~4x, so the gate is parallel leaching strings + outfall, not salt.
caveats: 7,000 t not stated as working vs total gas
5 yr may include commissioning slack of a first-of-kind project; boom-era caverns leached faster
break_this: Show either (a) SaltHy's working-gas figure (if 7,000 t is total, R09's 55 becomes ~80), or (b) a German cavern from 2006-14 whose leaching took >3 yr, or any H2 cavern leaching that has already started.
